definitions.explanation: Hanging laundry to dry inside the house rather than outdoors. Common during rainy season, winter, or in apartments without balconies.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{室内干|しつないぼ}しにする。
examples.english: On rainy days, I dry the laundry indoors.

examples.japanese: {室内干|しつないぼ}しだと{乾|かわ}きにくい。
examples.english: Laundry is hard to dry when hung indoors.

examples.japanese: {梅雨|つゆ}の{時期|じき}は{室内干|しつないぼ}しが{続|つづ}くので、{除湿機|じょしつき}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: During the rainy season, indoor drying continues for days, so a dehumidifier is essential.

notes:
Hanging laundry to dry inside the home, typically on a drying rack or pole. Very common in Japan due to frequent rain, limited balcony space in apartments, and concerns about pollen ({花粉|かふん}) or PM2.5.

ETYMOLOGY:
Composed of {室内|しつない} (indoors) + {干|ほ}し (drying).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {室内干|しつないぼ}しにする: to dry laundry indoors
- {室内干|しつないぼ}し{用|よう}の{洗剤|せんざい}: detergent for indoor drying
- {室内干|しつないぼ}し{用|よう}の{物干|ものほ}し: indoor drying rack

CONTRAST:
- {外干|そとぼ}し: drying laundry outdoors
- {天日干|てんぴぼ}し: sun-drying outdoors

NOTE:
Indoor drying can cause a musty smell ({生乾|なまがわ}きの{臭|にお}い) if not done properly. Using a {除湿機|じょしつき} (dehumidifier) or {扇風機|せんぷうき} (fan) helps speed up drying.
